title: Scheme Parser: Tokenize and Recursive Descent to S-Expressions
description: Two-stage parser: tokenize (regex) splits source into tokens; parse_tokens (recursive descent) builds nested Python lists. parse_atom converts tokens: #t/#f -> bool, quoted strings -> str, int/float -> numbers, else symbol (string). parse_sexp composes both. Demo: (+ 1 2) -> ['+', 1, 2]; (define x 42) -> ['define', 'x', 42]. (lambda (x) (* x x)) -> ['lambda', ['x'], ['*', 'x', 'x']]; (if #t 1 0) -> ['if', True, 1, 0]. (let ((x 5)) (+ x 1)) -> ['let', [['x', 5]], ['+', 'x', 1]].
source: draft: omp free model + edit: codex

steps.description: tokenize: regex pattern matches quoted strings, parentheses, or non-whitespace/non-paren/non-quote sequences. re.findall returns flat token list.
parse_atom: #t -> True, #f -> False, quoted string -> stripped string, try int, try float, else return token as symbol string. Numbers/booleans become Python values early.

parse_tokens: consumes tokens list as mutable queue (pop(0)). '(' starts list: builds result list recursively until ')', consumes ')'. ')' alone is error. ''' shorthand -> ['quote', parse_tokens(tokens)]. Else parse_atom.
Recursive descent: '(' triggers new list, each recursive call parses one element. tokens list mutates (pop(0)) so each call sees remaining tokens. Base cases: atom or ')' or '''.
parse_sexp: composes tokenize + parse_tokens. Single entry point.
Demo examples: arithmetic, define, lambda, if, let. Each printed as source => parsed Python representation.

steps.question: In (let ((x 5)) (+ x 1)), why does the parsed result have ['let', [['x', 5]], ['+', 'x', 1]] with double brackets around x 5?
steps.answer: The outer list is the let form. The first child is the bindings list: each binding is a two-element list [name, value]. So [['x', 5]] means one binding: x=5. The second child is the body ['+', 'x', 1].

steps.description: Output: each example source => parsed nested list. (+ 1 2) => ['+', 1, 2]; (define x 42) => ['define', 'x', 42]. (lambda (x) (* x x)) => ['lambda', ['x'], ['*', 'x', 'x']]; (if #t 1 0) => ['if', True, 1, 0]. (let ((x 5)) (+ x 1)) => ['let', [['x', 5]], ['+', 'x', 1]].
